api.description: Connect your own systems: API keys for the WallX Play REST API, and webhooks that tell your systems when something happens.
api.notInPlanTitle: The API and webhooks are not included in your plan
api.notInPlanBody: The API and webhooks are part of the Enterprise plan. Contact WallX to connect building management, alarm or reporting systems.
api.noPermission: Only members who can manage API keys (owners and admins) can create keys and webhooks. You can read the API reference below.

keys.title: API keys
keys.intro: Each key belongs to this organization and can only do what its scopes allow. Treat keys like passwords.
keys.name: Name
keys.nameHint: Where it is used, e.g. “Building management system”.
keys.revokeBody: Systems using this key stop working at once. This cannot be undone; create a new key if needed.
keys.showOnce: Copy the key now and store it safely. WallX Play does not keep it and cannot show it again.

scopes.screens_read: see screens, their status and emergencies

hooks.title: Webhooks
hooks.intro: WallX Play sends a signed HTTPS request to your address when the selected events happen.
hooks.urlHint: An https:// address on the internet that accepts POST requests.
hooks.secretOnce: Copy the signing secret now and use it to check the X-WallX-Signature header. It is not shown again; the old secret stops working.
hooks.deleteBody: No more events will be sent to {{url}}.

events.approval_decided: a publish request was approved or rejected
events.sensor_alert: a sensor reading crossed a rule
events.sensor_recovered: a sensor reading is back to normal

ref.title: API reference
ref.intro: Base address: {{base}}. Send the key in the Authorization header as “Bearer wxp_…”. Requests and responses are JSON.
ref.limits: Calls count against your plan’s daily limit (resets at 00:00 UTC). Errors come back as {"error", "message"} with the usual HTTP status codes: 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 429.
ref.webhooksBody: Each request is a JSON POST with id, event, createdAt, organization, data and link. Check the X-WallX-Signature header with your signing secret and ignore requests older than 5 minutes. Answer with any 2xx status; other answers are retried up to 3 times.

endpoints.me: This key, its organization and today’s usage
endpoints.screens: All screens with status, online state and versions
endpoints.emergency: Start an override: name, content (message or playlist), target, durationMinutes
endpoints.plays: Proof-of-play report (needs proof-of-play in the plan)
endpoints.uptime: Screen uptime and errors (needs screen diagnostics in the plan)

admin.description: Which organizations use the public API and webhooks. Counts only: customers’ keys and webhook addresses stay private.
admin.none: No organization uses the API or webhooks yet.
admin.note: Calls are counted per UTC day ({{day}}). “Not in plan” means keys or webhooks exist but the plan no longer includes them, so they are refused.
